paragraphs: Cybersecurity researcher working on the security of cross-chain systems and on AI for security. I am an M.Tech student at IIT Patna and a Junior Researcher in its Cybersecurity Lab, where I build testbeds that reproduce real bridge exploits and study how they could have been caught.

I like reading systems for what they assume rather than what they do, and asking what happens when an adversary does not share those assumptions. Outside research I play CTFs with team Enigma Hunters, design challenges, and teach security in English and Bengali.

researchInterests.title: Research Focus
researchInterests.statement: I study how cross-chain systems fail when verifiers, signers or relayers do not behave as their security argument assumes, and how AI agents can help detect, explain and respond to those failures. A second thread asks how far LLM judgments about security can be trusted.
areas: Reliability of LLMs in security analysis
researchInterests.futureGoals: Moving cross-chain security from after-the-fact postmortems to in-time detection and bounded, auditable response.

projects.title: Crucible
projects.description: A CLI-first, modular testbed for EVM bridge security research. It forks chains at historical blocks and reruns exploits deterministically, with structured run artifacts and a plugin SDK for attack, bridge and LLM-agent plugins. Ships with benchmark reproductions of the Wormhole, Nomad, Poly Network, Horizon, BNB Bridge and Multichain incidents.
projects.cv: Modular, CLI-first testbed for EVM cross-chain bridge security research: forks chains at historical blocks, replays exploits deterministically, records run artifacts with integrity hashes, and offers a plugin SDK for attack, bridge and LLM-agent plugins. Benchmarks for six incidents, including Wormhole, Nomad and Poly Network.

research.title: Beyond F1: A Study of LLM Reliability in Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection
research.description: Evaluates 14 LLMs from seven model families on 54 Solidity contracts under four prompting techniques. Model choice matters far more than prompting strategy, small open-source models flag vulnerabilities in every contract, and more inference-time reasoning does not reliably help: one model's F1 fell 11.5% with extended thinking enabled.
research.tldr: Across 14 LLMs, model choice matters more than prompting, and more reasoning does not always help.

research.title: Beyond Text: Nefarious Actors Harnessing LLMs for Strategic Advantage
research.description: This study explores how malicious actors exploit Large Language Models (LLMs) for cyber threats beyond conventional uses. Through literature review, case studies, and real-world analysis, it examines LLM-driven deception, social engineering, and cybercrimes such as phishing, password cracking, and malware propagation, highlighting emerging security challenges.
research.tldr: How attackers use LLMs for deception, phishing, password cracking and malware.

research.venue: International Conference on Innovations in Cybersecurity and Data Science (ICICDS), Springer
research.authors: S. Arjun, D. Majumdar, A. Z. Nabin, A. K. Sharma, S. M. Raheman
research.title: Beyond Copy–Pasting—Contextualizing LLMs for Secure Code Generation
research.description: This study evaluates security vulnerabilities in code generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) and copilots, emphasizing the need for strategic contextualization in secure coding practices. Through qualitative analysis, it assesses risks and proposes actionable strategies to help developers fine-tune LLMs for secure code generation.
research.tldr: LLM-generated code carries vulnerabilities; contextualization reduces them.

research.venue: 9th International Conference on Advanced Computing and Communication Systems (ICACCS), IEEE
research.title: Shadow ARP-ing for ARP Poisoning Detection
research.description: This study addresses ARP spoofing, a longstanding network security threat enabling attacks such as MITM and DDoS. It proposes an automated OS-based monitoring technique to detect ARP poisoning in real time, reducing reliance on manual ARP table checks and minimizing detection delays.
research.tldr: Automated, OS-level ARP cache monitoring that detects ARP poisoning as it happens.

classic.role: M.Tech student and Junior Researcher, Cybersecurity Lab, IIT Patna
classic.printHeader: Durjoy Majumdar | Cross-chain security & AI | IIT Patna
bio: I'm a second-year M.Tech student in Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Patna and a Junior Researcher in its Cybersecurity Lab, where I work with Dr. Somnath Tripathy.

Most of my work comes back to one question: what happens when a system's trust assumptions meet an adversary who doesn't share them? I first asked it of ARP, then of LLM-generated code, and now of cross-chain bridges, which fail when verifiers, signers or relayers stop behaving the way the security argument assumes. I'm working on AI agents that detect and explain these failures, and I built Crucible, a testbed that replays historical bridge exploits on forked chains, so that this work can be tested against real attacks.
I also study the other side of AI in security: how attackers use LLMs, and how far LLM judgments about code and smart contracts can be trusted.
